TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which U.S. president is featured on the penny coin?
expl: Abraham Lincoln has been featured on the U.S. one-cent coin, known as the penny, since 1909. The design was introduced to mark the 100th anniversary of his birth. Lincoln also appears on the five-dollar bill and on Mount Rushmore.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Who was the Egyptian queen who famously aligned with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony?
expl: Cleopatra VII was the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt. She formed powerful alliances with Roman leaders Julius Caesar and later Mark Antony, and her story has been immortalized in literature and film.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: On what day do Americans celebrate Independence Day?
expl: Americans celebrate Independence Day on July 4th every year. It marks the day in 1776 when the Declaration of Independence was adopted, declaring freedom from Great Britain. Families typically celebrate with cookouts, parades, and fireworks.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Who was the leader of the Cuban Revolution?
expl: Fidel Castro led the Cuban Revolution that overthrew the Batista government in 1959. He then ruled Cuba as Prime Minister and later President for nearly five decades, becoming one of the world's longest-serving heads of state.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which country was formerly known as Persia?
expl: Iran was formerly known as Persia. The country officially changed its name from Persia to Iran in 1935 at the request of its then-ruler Reza Shah, who wanted to reflect the Aryan heritage of the Iranian people.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which famous American document was signed on July 4, 1776?
expl: The Declaration of Independence was signed on July 4, 1776, announcing that the thirteen American colonies were free from British rule. It was mainly written by Thomas Jefferson. Americans celebrate this important day every year as Independence Day with parades and fireworks.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which city was the capital of the Byzantine Empire?
expl: Constantinople, modern-day Istanbul in Turkey, served as the capital of the Byzantine Empire for over a thousand years. Founded by Emperor Constantine I in 330 AD, the city fell to the Ottoman Turks in 1453.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Who assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand, triggering World War I?
expl: Gavrilo Princip, a Bosnian Serb nationalist, assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914. This event set off a chain reaction of political decisions that led to the outbreak of World War I.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: The ancient city of Carthage was located in which modern-day country?
expl: Carthage was an ancient Phoenician city-state located in what is now northeastern Tunisia. It was one of the most powerful cities of the ancient world before being destroyed by Rome at the end of the Third Punic War in 146 BC.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which famous nurse is known as the founder of modern nursing?
expl: Florence Nightingale is considered the founder of modern nursing. During the Crimean War, she dramatically improved sanitation and saved thousands of lives. She established the first secular nursing school in the world at St Thomas Hospital in London.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Who was the first man to walk on the Moon?
expl: Neil Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon on July 20, 1969, during NASA's Apollo 11 mission. He famously declared 'That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind' as he stepped onto the lunar surface.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which pharaoh built the Great Pyramid of Giza?
expl: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built by Pharaoh Khufu, also known as Cheops, around 2560 BC. It is the oldest and largest of the three pyramids in the Giza pyramid complex and is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which war was fought between the North and South in the United States from 1861 to 1865?
expl: The American Civil War was fought from 1861 to 1865 between the Union (Northern states) and the Confederacy (Southern states). The primary cause was the disagreement over slavery. The Union won, and slavery was abolished throughout the United States.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which document begins with the words 'We the People'?
expl: The U.S. Constitution famously begins with the words 'We the People of the United States, in Order to form a more perfect Union.' It was signed on September 17, 1787, and is the supreme law of the land. The original document is kept at the National Archives in Washington, D.C.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Who was the last Tsar of Russia?
expl: Nicholas II was the last Tsar of Russia, reigning from 1894 until his abdication in 1917. Following the Russian Revolution, he and his family were executed by the Bolsheviks in 1918. His reign saw Russia's involvement in both the Russo-Japanese War and World War I.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: The Battle of Waterloo took place in which country?
expl: The Battle of Waterloo took place on June 18, 1815, near the town of Waterloo in present-day Belgium. Napoleon Bonaparte was decisively defeated by the allied forces led by the Duke of Wellington and Field Marshal Blücher, ending the Napoleonic Wars.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which famous ship sank in the North Atlantic Ocean in April 1912?
expl: The Titanic was a huge British passenger ship that sank on April 15, 1912, after hitting an iceberg on its very first voyage from England to New York. It was once thought to be unsinkable. The sinking became one of the most famous shipwrecks in history.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which American inventor is famous for creating the first practical light bulb?
expl: Thomas Edison is famous for inventing the first practical incandescent light bulb in 1879. He held over 1,000 patents and also helped develop the phonograph and motion picture camera. His New Jersey laboratory is often called America's first 'invention factory.'

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Who invented the printing press around 1440?
expl: Johannes Gutenberg invented the movable-type printing press around 1440 in Mainz, Germany. This revolutionary invention made the mass production of books possible, facilitating the spread of the Renaissance, Reformation, and Scientific Revolution.
